payload.name: Event-date retrieval from event memories only
payload.description: When a question asks when an event happened (e.g., when did X give/get Y for Z) and initial retrieval returns a non-event memory mentioning the item, do not use that memory's timestamp as the answer. Apply before answering.
content: If a 'when did X give/get Y' question retrieves a non-event memory (preference, relationship, profile) mentioning Y, treat its world_start as unreliable for the event date; search for an event memory about the giving using generic terms such as 'gave', 'gift', 'received', or the object category.
Run a structured or hybrid search restricted to memory_kind 'event' (or predicate 'gift'/'gave') if the first search did not return one, and answer using the event memory's world_start.
Stop once an event memory directly describing the transaction is found; do not infer the date from preferences or relationship memories.

solves: When a question asks for the date of an event (e.g., when did someone give/receive something), the agent may answer with the timestamp of a non-event memory (preference, relationship, profile) that merely mentions the item, confusing a memory's recorded date with the actual event date. This skill guides the agent to treat only event-memory timestamps as evidence and to search for the underlying event using gift/give terms when the initial retrieval only surfaces non-event mentions.
